deck_title: Enterprise Interactive UI Motion Stack: Rive 48KB Vector Bone State Machine & Blend Tree (b_rive = b_0/(1+u), 1.0000x Lock) vs Lottie Linear JSON vs Pre-Rendered WebM Alpha Video

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Enterprise Interactive UI Motion stack evaluation (compiling 17 interactive states, 2D pointer-tracking IK, and audio-amplitude lip-sync into a single 48 KB .riv vector bone state machine with 60fps C++/WASM blend-tree cross-fading so amortized per-state cost b_rive(u) = b_0 / (1 + u) reaches 0.5000 at u = 1.0, locking B_active / B_rive = 1.0000x across all 17 interactive tiers u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive pre-rendered multi-clip WebM alpha videos / raster Lottie JSONs (which suffer jarring interruption jump-cuts and inflate bundle/rework cost by 1 + u to 1.2500x at T4, 1.5000x at T8, and 2.0000x at T16 across 16/17 tiers) and 64-frame blend-tree quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Interactive AI Copilot mascots (idle -> listening -> thinking -> speaking -> interrupted) with continuous 2D cursor gaze and audio-amplitude lip-sync
Automotive HMI digital instrument clusters, gamified mobile onboarding, and luxury brand interactive product cards requiring <50 KB bundle size at 60fps
Runtime theme color-slot binding and dynamic multilingual text runs inside vector skeletal rigs without re-exporting from After Effects
not_for: Photorealistic live-action human spokesperson footage (use AI Avatar / WebM Alpha)
Simple 2-state CSS opacity/transform button hovers (use native CSS transitions)
Full-scene 360-degree CAD product inspection (use Three.js / R3F + 3DGS)

dark_box.lead: MIT original code. Synthetic educational scene; local checks reproduced. No production, physics, or neural inference certification.
